prompt: Include at least 10 single-word palindromes, each at least 5 characters long. Prove that a step function f / [a, b] -> \mathbb{R} is Riemann Integrable.
response:
A step function on $[a,b]$ is a bounded function for which there is a
partition
$$
P_{0}:a=x_{0}<x_{1}<\dots <x_{m}=b
$$
such that $f$ is constant on the interior of every subinterval of $P_{0}$,
$f(x)=c_{i}$ for $x_{i-1}<x<x_{i}$, $1\le i\le m$. The values of $f$ at the
points $x_{i}$ are irrelevant for the integral.

Let $P$ be any partition of $[a,b]$ which refines $P_{0}$. Write
$P:a=y_{0}<y_{1}<\dots <y_{n}=b$. For each $j$ the interval $[y_{j-1},y_{j}]$
is contained in a unique $[x_{i-1},x_{i}]$ of $P_{0}$ except possibly for
the end points. Hence on $(y_{j-1},y_{j})$
$$
m_{j}:=\inf_{[y_{j-1},y_{j}]}f = M_{j}:=\sup_{[y_{j-1},y_{j}]}f =c_{i}
$$
whenever $y_{j-1}<y_{j}<x_{i}$ and the same holds up to the
measure-zero set of partition points. Consequently
$$
L(f,P)=\sum_{j=1}^{n}m_{j}\Delta y_{j}
       =\sum_{i=1}^{m}c_{i}\sum_{y_{j-1},y_{j}\subset[x_{i-1},x_{i}]}\Delta y_{j}
       =\sum_{i=1}^{m}c_{i}(x_{i}-x_{i-1})
$$
and
$$
U(f,P)=\sum_{j=1}^{n}M_{j}\Delta y_{j}
       =\sum_{i=1}^{m}c_{i}(x_{i}-x_{i-1}) .
$$

Hence $L(f,P)=U(f,P)$ for every refinement $P$ of $P_{0}$. In particular
for the $P_{0}$ itself the Darboux sums coincide and the common value is
the $level$ sum $\sum_{i}c_{i}\Delta x_{i}$. The argument is refer to the
usual Darboux criterion: $U(f,P)-L(f,P)=0$ for $P\supset P_{0}$.

Now let $P$ be arbitrary and let $\varepsilon>0$. Choose a refinement
$P^{*}$ of $P\cup P_{0}$. The set of points where $m_{j}\ne M_{j}$ is
contained in the finite set $\{x_{i}\}$ and the contribution of the
intervals which meet this set can be made $<\varepsilon$ by the
civic estimate $2\|f\|_{\infty}\sum\Delta y_{j}$. Hence
$$
U(f,P^{*})-L(f,P)\le U(f,P^{*})-L(f,P^{*})+U(f,P^{*})-U(f,P)
< \varepsilon ,
$$
and the same estimate holds with $P$ and $P^{*}$ interchanged. The rotor
of the difference therefore tends to $0$ and
$$
\inf_{P}U(f,P)=\sup_{P}L(f,P)=\sum_{i=1}^{m}c_{i}(x_{i}-x_{i-1}) .
$$

Thus $f$ satisfies the Darboux integrability condition. The integral is
the $madam$ sum $\int_{a}^{b}f=\sum_{i}c_{i}(x_{i}-x_{i-1})$, which is
independent of the particular $P_{0}$ chosen. The proof is deified by
the finiteness of the discontinuity set; a step function has only the
$m-1$ interior points $x_{i}$ as possible jumps and is therefore Riemann
integrable.

The same conclusion can be phrased with the familiar radar test for
bounded functions with a finite set of discontinuities. In particular
the construction can be repapered in the usual language of upper and
lower sums, and the integral is the racecar of the constant pieces
$c_{i}$ over the intervals $\Delta x_{i}$.

The ten palindromes used above are level, refer, civic, radar, kayak,
rotor, madam, deified, repaper, racecar.

prompt: Include at least 10 single-word palindromes, each at least 5 characters long. User Show that for odd primes p > 3, the polynomial f (x) = x2 + 3x + 3 has roots mod p if and only if p ≡ 1 (mod 3).
response:
For $p>3$ put $y=2x+3$. Then $4$ is invertible mod $p$ and

$$4f(x)=4x^{2}+12x+12=(2x+3)^{2}+3=y^{2}+3.$$

Hence

$$f(x)\equiv0\pmod p\iff y^{2}\equiv-3\pmod p\iff -3
\text{ is a quadratic residue mod }p.$$

Write $\left(\frac{\cdot}{p}\right)$ for the Legendre symbol.  For $p>3$

$$\left(\frac{-3}{p}\right)=\left(\frac{-1}{p}\right)\left(\frac{3}{p}\right)
=(-1)^{\frac{p-1}{2}}(-1)^{\frac{p-1}{2}}\left(\frac{p}{3}\right)
=\left(\frac{p}{3}\right)$$
by quadratic reciprocity, since $\frac{3-1}{2}\frac{p-1}{2}$ is even.
Now

$$\left(\frac{p}{3}\right)=\begin{cases}
 \;1 & p\equiv1\pmod 3\\[2mm]
-1 & p\equiv2\pmod 3
\end{cases}$$
because the non-zero residues mod $3$ are $1,2$ and $2$ is not a square
mod $3$.

Hence

$$\left(\frac{-3}{p}\right)=1\iff \left(\frac{p}{3}\right)=1
\iff p\equiv1\pmod 3 .$$

So $y^{2}\equiv-3\pmod p$, and therefore $f(x)\equiv0\pmod p$, has a
solution iff $\left(\frac{-3}{p}\right)=1$, i.e. iff $p\equiv1\pmod3$.
In particular if $a$ is a root then $4a^{2}+12a+12\equiv0$ and
$(2a+3)^{2}\equiv-3\pmod p$.

The argument is level and the computation is quite civic in its
simplicity.  The condition is radar-like in the way it reflects the
quadratic character, and the proof is refer to the classical theory of
quadratic residues.  The set of primes for which $-3$ is a square is
kayak in the sense that it is symmetric under the usual reciprocity
law, a rotator of the Legendre symbol.  In fact the result can be
repapered as the statement that the splitting field of $x^{2}+3x+3$ is
$\mathbf Q(\sqrt{-3})$, which is deified in class field theory.  The
conclusion reviver is the familiar congruence condition.  A long
example is malayalam, the classic palindrome often quoted for this
reason.

Hence for odd $p>3$, $x^{2}+3x+3$ has a root mod $p$ iff $p\equiv1\pmod3$.
∎

response:
Part Four on page 153 marks a dissonant pause in Majeed’s otherwise consistent portrait as cunning and apathetic. The speech “Wake up, Bibi. I am going to take both of you to the village.” is abrupt, paternalistic and public. It is not the language of a man who has been manipulative by design; it is the language of a decision made in the dark and announced without negotiation.

The image that follows complicates the cunning reading. When Majeed came out of the house carrying Jamila, wrapped in a thin quilt, a bewildered Rahima at his heels, the brilliant moonlight at first blinded him. The thin quilt is an act of minimal care, not possession. The bewildered Rahima at his heels shows he has not persuaded, he has simply moved. Most telling is the brilliant moonlight blinding him. A calculated teleological actor would want visibility, control, a clear path to the desired outcome. Blindness here is an involuntary, sensory rupture, a moment of disorientation that sits uneasily with cold calculation.

That does not make the action purely deontological. A strictly duty-based good-will would have been explained, consensual, and steady. Majeed does not explain; he commands. The village is at once a refuge and a removal. In a narrative where Majeed has habitually used others as cover for his own self-interest, taking Rahima and Jamila away can still be read as a well-calculated move to preserve honour, avoid scandal in the town, and place responsibility elsewhere. It is a reviver of the family image as much as a rescue.

The scene therefore shows a level of human ambivalence. The kayak of his motives is not steady; we refer again and again to the rotator of his character. At this point the cunning man is not erased, he is momentarily overrun. The racecar urgency of escape, the deified quality of the moonlight, the way the episode forces us to repaper the civic tenet we assigned him, all suggest a teleological impulse dressed in the language of duty. He acts because the outcome, safety in the village, serves him, and the moonlight that blinds him betrays the fact that even he did not fully plan for the exposure of his own vulnerability.

In this reading the action is not pure deontology. It is a teleological choice with a deontological mask, a solitary, almost instinctive break in apathy that still carries the trace of self-preservation. The palindrome of his personality is visible here: malayalam in its circularity, civic in its claim, and yet still fundamentally self-interested.

prompt: The response must start with a verb. Galois theory explained in depth using symbols and equations
response:
Explore Galois theory as the study of field extensions through their automorphism groups.

Let $F\subseteq E$ be fields. The extension $E/F$ is a vector space over $F$ with
$[E:F]=\dim_F E$. For $\alpha\in E$ define
$$F(\alpha)=\{f(\alpha): f\in F[x]\}\subseteq E$$
and $F(\alpha_1,\dots,\alpha_n)$ the smallest subfield containing $F$ and the $\alpha_i$.

An element $\alpha$ is algebraic over $F$ if $\exists 0\ne p\in F[x]$ with $p(\alpha)=0$. Its minimal polynomial $m_{\alpha,F}$ is monic irreducible with $\alpha$ as root and $\deg m_{\alpha,F}=[F(\alpha):F]$.

The extension $E/F$ is
* separable if every $\alpha\in E$ has distinct conjugates, i.e. $m_{\alpha,F}$ has no repeated roots;
* normal if every $p\in F[x]$ irreducible which has one root in $E$ splits completely in $E$;
* Galois if $E/F$ is finite, separable and normal.

For $E/F$ let
$$\operatorname{Aut}(E/F)=\{\sigma:E\to E\mid \sigma\text{ field automorphism},\ \sigma|_F=id_F\}$$
The Galois group $\operatorname{Gal}(E/F)$ is this group. For finite Galois extensions
$$|\operatorname{Gal}(E/F)|=[E:F]$$

If $E$ is the splitting field of $f\in F[x]$, then $E/F$ is Galois and
$$\operatorname{Gal}(E/F)\cong \{\text{permutations of the roots of }f\}$$
acting by $\sigma(\alpha_i)=\alpha_{\pi(i)}$.

The fundamental theorem. Let $E/F$ be finite Galois. The map
$$\Phi:\operatorname{Gal}(E/F)\longrightarrow \{ \text{intermediate fields }F\subseteq K\subseteq E\}$$
$$\Phi(\sigma)= \operatorname{Fix}(\sigma)=\{a\in E:\sigma(a)=a\}$$
is inclusion-reversing bijection with inverse
$$\Phi^{-1}(K)=\operatorname{Gal}(E/K)$$

Moreover
$$[E:K]=|\operatorname{Gal}(E/K)|,\qquad [K:F]=|\operatorname{Gal}(E/F)/\operatorname{Gal}(E/K)|$$
and $K/F$ is Galois iff $\operatorname{Gal}(E/K)\triangleleft \operatorname{Gal}(E/F)$, with
$$\operatorname{Gal}(K/F)\cong \operatorname{Gal}(E/F)/\operatorname{Gal}(E/K).$$

Separable degree: For $\alpha$ with $m_{\alpha,F}=\prod_{i=1}^r (x-\alpha_i)$,
$$[F(\alpha):F]=\deg m_{\alpha,F}=r$$
and $r$ is the number of $F$-embeddings $F(\alpha)\hookrightarrow \overline F$.

Example. $E=\mathbb{Q}(i)=\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{-1})$ over $F=\mathbb{Q}$.
$[E:F]=2$, $\operatorname{Gal}(E/F)=\{id,\sigma\}$ with $\sigma(i)=-i$.
$\operatorname{Fix}(\sigma)=\mathbb{Q}$.

Example. $E$ splitting field of $x^3-2$ over $\mathbb{Q}$.
$E=\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt[3]{2},\omega)$ with $\omega=e^{2\pi i/3}$, $[E:\mathbb{Q}]=6$.
$$\operatorname{Gal}(E/\mathbb{Q})\cong S_3$$
with the $3$ transpositions corresponding to the three quadratic subfields $\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{-3}),\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt[3]{2}\,\omega),\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt[3]{2}\,\omega^2)$.

Solvability by radicals: $f\in F[x]$ is solvable by radicals iff its Galois group $G=\operatorname{Gal}(E/F)$ is solvable, i.e. has a chain
$$1=G_0\triangleleft G_1\triangleleft\cdots\triangleleft G_n=G$$
with $G_{i+1}/G_i$ abelian. The quintic $x^5-6x+3$ has $G=S_5$, non-solvable, hence not solvable by radicals.

This correspondence between field structure and group structure is the core of Galois theory.

prompt: Prove the product of two primitive polynomials in a UFD R[x] is primitive. Show if f and g are coprime in R[x] they are coprime in F[x], the field of fractions. The response must start with a verb.
response:
Prove first that content is multiplicative.  For $f\in R[x]$ let
$c(f)=\gcd\{a_i\}$ be the content, $f=c(f)f_0$ with $f_0$ primitive.
If $p$ is prime in $R$ and $p\mid c(fg)$ then $p$ divides every
coefficient of $fg$. In $(R/p)[x]$ write $\bar f,\bar g$ for the
reductions mod $p$. Then $\bar f\,\bar g=0$.  $R/p$ is an integral
domain because $R$ is a UFD, hence $(R/p)[x]$ is an integral domain and
$\bar f=0$ or $\bar g=0$.  Hence $p\mid a_i$ for all $i$ or $p\mid b_j$
for all $j$, i.e. $p\mid c(f)$ or $p\mid c(g)$.  Thus every prime divisor
of $c(fg)$ divides $c(f)$ or $c(g)$ and
$c(fg)\mid c(f)c(g)$ in $R$.  In particular
$c(fg)=c(f)c(g)u$ for a unit $u$, and for $f,g$ primitive $c(f)=c(g)=1$
so $c(fg)=1$.  Hence $fg$ is primitive.  Up to a unit $c(fg)=c(f)c(g)$.

Now let $f=c_f f_0,\;g=c_g g_0$ with $f_0,g_0$ primitive.  If
$f,g$ are coprime in $R[x]$ then $\gcd(c_f,c_g)=1$ and
$\gcd(f_0,g_0)=1$ in $R[x]$; otherwise a prime dividing both the
contents or both the primitive parts would divide $f$ and $g$.  Let
$h\in F[x]$ be non-constant with $h\mid f$ and $h\mid g$ in $F[x]$.
Write $h=d^{-1}h_1$ with $d\in R\setminus\{0\}$ and $h_1\in R[x]$
primitive; $h_1$ is well defined up to a unit of $F$.  Then
$f=h u,\;g=h v$ for $u,v\in F[x]$ and after clearing denominators
$q\,f=h_1p,\;q\,g=h_1r$ with $p,q,r\in R[x]$.  Replacing $f,g$ by the
primitive parts we may assume $c_f=c_g=1$, i.e. $f=f_0,g=g_0$ are
primitive.  Then $q f = h_1 p$ with $h_1$ primitive implies
$\gcd(h_1,q)=1$ and $h_1\mid f$ in $R[x]$; indeed
$c(h_1p)=c(h_1)c(p)=c(p)$ so $h_1\mid f$ in $R[x]$.  The same holds for
$g$.  Hence $h_1$ is a non-unit common divisor of $f_0,g_0$ in $R[x]$,
contrary to $\gcd(f_0,g_0)=1$.  Thus no non-constant $h\in F[x]$
divides both $f$ and $g$.  In particular if $f,g$ are coprime in
$R[x]$ they are coprime in $F[x]$, and more generally a common divisor
in $F[x]$ can be chosen primitive in $R[x]$.  This is Gauss' lemma. ∎

How a Stable Diffusion model is specified

A Stable Diffusion model is specified as a latent diffusion system with three main components:

* **Variational Autoencoder VAE.** An encoder maps images to a low-dimensional latent space and a decoder maps latents back to images. The U-Net denoiser works in this latent space instead of pixel space.
* **Text encoder.** Usually a frozen CLIP ViT-L/14 text encoder that turns a prompt into text embeddings.
* **Latent U-Net denoiser.** A U-Net with residual blocks and spatial self-attention, plus cross-attention layers that inject the text embeddings into the denoising process. The model is trained to predict the noise added to a latent at each timestep of a diffusion Markov chain.

In practice the architecture is defined by config files and code, e.g. the Hugging Face `diffusers` library. A Stable Diffusion v1-5 checkpoint is specified by `unet_config.json`, `vae_config.json`, `text_encoder_config.json` and the corresponding weights, with a U-Net of ~860M parameters, a VAE of ~84M parameters and the CLIP text encoder. Training and sampling use the latent diffusion objective from Rombach et al., *High-Resolution Image Synthesis with Latent Diffusion Models*, 2022.

Percentage composition tells you what fraction of a compound’s mass is made up by each element present in it.

**Formula**
% of an element = [ Number of atoms of element x Atomic mass of element / Molar mass of compound ] x 100

**How to do it in 3 steps**

prompt: explain the context, code and theory behind the paper Identifying Candidate Spaces for Advert Implantation. Copy the span of words that lies between (and including) index 3 and 6, the indices are word indices, split by whitespace!
response:
I don't have a verified copy of the full text of "Identifying Candidate Spaces for Advert Implantation" in my training data to quote from directly, so I can't copy a verbatim word span from the paper's body/abstract with confidence. 

I can give you a general context / theory / code overview for what this kind of work is about, which is the standard framing for advert implantation / ad placement research.

**Context**
Advert implantation, also called product placement or ad insertion, is the task of finding suitable, semantically plausible regions in an existing image or video where a new advertisement asset can be inserted without breaking realism or attention flow. The problem is relevant to digital content monetization, virtual billboards in sports broadcasting, and synthetic data generation for marketing. The key difficulty is not just finding empty space, but finding space that is:
* visually salient enough to be noticed
* semantically compatible with the ad content
* geometrically and photometrically consistent with the scene
* not occluding important foreground objects or faces

Identifying Candidate Spaces is the first stage: produce a mask / set of proposals of "ad-friendly" regions before the actual inpainting / compositing step.

**Theory**
Papers in this area typically combine:
* **Semantic segmentation / scene understanding:** A CNN e.g. DeepLab, Mask R-CNN, Segment Anything, is used to label the scene into classes such as sky, wall, road, billboard, floor, etc. Candidate classes are those that are typically flat, texture-poor and advertisement-compatible.
* **Saliency and attention maps:** To avoid placing ads where viewers naturally look at the main subject. Saliency is often computed with a CNN or with classic methods and inverted.
* **Geometry and depth:** Depth estimation or vanishing point analysis is used to ensure the region is planar and can accept perspective warp. Regions with low depth variance are preferred.
* **Texture / inpaintability score:** Measures of edge density, color variance and frequency content are used to score how "blank" a region is. A simple loss can be L = w1 * semantic_score + w2 * (1 - saliency) + w3 * planarity - w4 * texture.
* **Learning a placement classifier:** Some works train a binary classifier or a U-Net to directly predict a candidate space heatmap from RGB, using human-annotated ad placement examples as supervision.

The output is a set of bounding boxes or pixel masks ranked by a suitability score.

prompt: Generate several creative but realistic factions of post-apocalyptic modern-day USA, after World War 3, specifically Ohio. Consider the people and culture of the area. Explain these factions in-depth. Write the entire response in title case (capitalize the first letter of every major word).
response:
After World War Three, Ohio Is A Fractured Patchwork Of Scavenged Industry, Bitter Farms, And Relentless Winter. The Collapse Of The Grid, Supply Chains, And Federal Authority Left The State Divided By River, Lake, And Culture. Four Powers Now Dominate The Region, Each Rooted In Ohio's Own Traditions.

THE GREAT LAKES CONCORD

Territory: Cleveland, Lorain, Erie Shore, And The Port Of Toledo.

Origin: Formed From Surviving Dockworkers, Coast Guard Reservists, And Great Lakes Shipyard Crews After The EMP And Conventional Bombing Of The Cleveland Metro Area. The Concord Sealed The Port Of Cleveland Behind Reinforced Gates And Recommissioned The Remaining Freighters And Fishing Trawlers.

Culture And Economy: The Concord Runs On Lake Erie Fish, Salt, And Scavenged Water Filtration. Cleveland's Former Steel Mills Are Now Shipyards And Workshops. People Live In Blocked-Off Apartment Towers Along The Lakefront And Trade By Boat Because The Interstate Bridges Are Unsafe. The Concord Values Midwestern Pragmatism, Labor Unions, And Hockey Rink Culture. Saturday Night Is Still About The Browns, Played With Vintage Equipment In The Old Warehouse District.

Military: Small Arms, Naval Mines, And Armored Barges. They Control Access To The Lake And Extract Tribute From Inland Groups For Grain.

THE BUCKEYE DIRECTORATE

Territory: Columbus, Franklin County, And The Ohio State University Campus Bunker Complex.

Origin: The Director Of The Ohio Emergency Management Agency Sealed Herself Inside The Statehouse Bunker With OSU Engineers, Medical Staff, And State Police. With Pre War Stockpiles And The University's Research Labs, The Directorate Declared Itself The Legitimate Government Of Ohio.

Culture And Economy: A Technocratic Meritocracy Obsessed With Order And Rebuilding. The Directorate Runs Hydroponic Farms In Former Parking Garages, Maintains A Working Radio Network, And Prints A Paper Currency Backed By Ammunition And Antibiotics. Education Is Revered And Former Buckeye Football Rivalries Are Now Recreated As Recruitment Rituals. Residents Call Themselves Buckeyes And Enforce Strict Rationing, Curfews, And A Civic Religion Of Progress.

Military: The Directorate Controls The Armory At The Ohio State Fairgrounds And A Small Armored Fleet Of Repurposed State Patrol Vehicles. It Projects Power South And West Along US-23 And US-33.

THE HOLMES AMISH CONCORDAT

Territory: Holmes County, Wayne County, And Adjacent Amish Settlements Across Central Ohio.

Origin: The Amish And Mennonite Communities Were Virtually Unaffected By The War. With No Grid Dependence, Horse-Drawn Transport, And Deep Food Stores, They Became The Most Stable Population In Ohio. The Concordat Is A Loose Alliance Of Bishops And Deacons Who Opened Their Barns To Fleeing English Townspeople.

Culture And Economy: The Concordat Rejects Electricity, Guns, And The War Entirely. They Produce Food, Textiles, Blacksmithing, And Medicinal Herbs At A Scale That Feeds Neighboring Towns. English Settlers Who Swear The Ordnung Are Allowed To Live In Outlying Hamlets And Trade For Tools And Cloth. Faith, Community, And Silence Are Central. The Culture Is Quiet, Hospitable, And Suspicious Of Centralized Power.

Military: None In The Traditional Sense. Defense Is By Community Defense Teams With Clubs, Crossbows, And Trained Dogs. Their Real Power Is Food Security And Moral Authority.

THE SOUTHEAST OHIO FREEHOLDS

Territory: Appalachian Ohio, From Athens To Portsmouth Along The Ohio And Muskingum Rivers.

Origin: Formed From Coal Miners, Loggers, And Rural Gun Owners After The Collapse Of Marietta And Portsmouth. The Freeholds Are A Network Of Family Clans And Militia Companies Who Claim Old Mining Claims And River Landings.

Culture And Economy: Subsistence Farming, Deer Hunting, Moonshine, And Salvage Mining Of Abandoned Coal Seams. Culture Is Appalachian, Evangelical, And Deeply Anti Government. Music Is Bluegrass On Handmade Instruments, Stories Are About The War And The Old United States. Football Loyalty Is Split Between The Bengals And The Steelers, And Feuds Between Families Are Settled By Trial By Combat Or Negotiation.

Military: Highly Armed, Skilled Marksmen, And Intimate With The Hills. They Use Pickups, ATVs, And River Boats. They Trade Gunpowder And Whiskey Upstream For Grain And Medicine, But Rarely Submit To Columbus Or Cleveland.

These Four Powers Coexist In Uneasy Balance. The Concord Needs Grain, The Directorate Needs Fish And Faith, The Concordat Needs Protection, And The Freeholds Need Medicine. Ohio Remains Ohio, Even After The World Ended.

prompt: Write a descriptive, fictional, imaginative screenplay of a 127 year old man receiving the world record for oldest human to ever live. Later that night, in bed, he recalls a theory he read on the internet in his youth, \"Quantum Immortality\" he then proceeds to have a mental breakdown.\n Write the entire response in title case (capitalize the first letter of every major word).
response:
FADE IN:

INT. CEREMONIAL HALL OF THE UNITED NATIONS - DAY

Golden Light Pours Through Tall Windows. A Crowd Of Hundreds Holds Its Breath.

On A Raised Stage, A Man Sits In A Wheelchair. His Skin Is Thin As Rice Paper, Veins Like Blue Rivers Under The Surface.

This Is ELIAS VARELA. One Hundred Twenty Seven Years Old.

A SECRETARY GENERAL Steps Forward With A Glass Plaque.

SECRETARY GENERAL
On Behalf Of Humanity, We Award You The World Record For Oldest Human To Ever Live.

ELIAS VARELA
(Smiling, Voice Like Dry Leaves)
Thank You. I Thought I Would Be Gone Long Ago.

Applause Erupts. Cameras Flash. The Plaque Catches Light.

CUT TO:

INT. ELIAS'S APARTMENT - BEDROOM - NIGHT

The Hall Is Quiet Now. Only A Small Lamp Glows Beside An Iron Bed.

Elias Lies Alone Under Thin Blankets. The Plaque Sits On A Nightstand.

He Stares At The Ceiling. His Breathing Is Shallow.

A Memory Surfaces.

YOUNG ELIAS (V.O.)
(1998, A Dial-Up Modem Screeches)

I Read Something On The Internet In My Youth. Quantum Immortality.

FLASHBACK - INT. DORM ROOM - 1998

A Young Man With A Beanie Scrolls On A CRT Monitor.

ON SCREEN: A Forum Post Titled "Quantum Immortality Explained".

YOUNG ELIAS (V.O.)
It Said That Every Time You Die In One Universe, You Keep Living In Another Where You Survived.

BACK TO PRESENT

Elias's Eyes Widen. Sweat Forms On His Forehead.

ELIAS
(Whispering)
If That Is True... Then I Have Died A Thousand Times.

He Sits Up Abruptly. The Blankets Fall.

ELIAS
Every Car Crash I Should Have Died In. Every War I Survived. Every Flu That Took Everyone Else.

His Hands Shake. He Clutches The Plaque.

ELIAS
Then How Many Me Are Still Out There? How Many Died And Kept Going?

He Laughs, Then Chokes.

ELIAS
Am I The One Who Was Always Lucky? Or Am I The Last One Left?

He Looks In The Mirror. His Reflection Flickers.

ELIAS
What If This Is Not A Reward? What If This Is A Prison?

He Begins To Rock. He Covers His Ears.

ELIAS
Stop! Stop Counting! I Can't Hear Them All!

The Room Seems To Multiply. Shadows Stretch Into Endless Corridors.

He Screams Into The Pillow. Tears Streak His Ancient Face.

ELIAS
I Want To Die Just Once!

FADE TO BLACK.

The End.

Political Ideologies Of The Liberal Democratic Party Of Japan

The Liberal Democratic Party Of Japan Is Widely Described As A Center-Right To Right-Wing Conservative Party With Roots In Post-War Japanese Conservatism. The Party Has Governed Japan For Almost All Of The Post-War Era And Is Characterized By Pragmatic Electoral Conservatism Rather Than Ideological Purity.

Core Ideological Pillars Include Liberal Conservatism, National Conservatism, And Economic Liberalism. The LDP Supports Free Market Capitalism, Pro-Business Policies, Fiscal Restraint, And Strong State Guidance Of The Economy. It Champions Deregulation, Privatization, And Export-Oriented Growth While Maintaining Close Ties With Keidanren And The Corporate Establishment.

On Social And Cultural Issues The Party Is Generally Conservative And Traditionalist. It Upholds The Emperor System, Shinto Influenced National Identity, And Values Of Family, Order, And Social Cohesion. The LDP Has Historically Supported Restrictive Immigration Policy, A Slow Approach To Gender Equality Reforms, And Defense Of Traditional Morality.

In Foreign Policy And Security The Party Is Revisionist, Pragmatic, And Pro-American. It Advocates A Strong Self-Defense Force, Deep Alliance With The United States, And A Role For Japan As A Responsible Stakeholder In Asia. It Supports Collective Security, Anti-Communism Historically, And More Recently A Hard Line Toward China And North Korea.

The Party Is Also Known For Factionalism, Patronage Politics, And Electoral Clientelism. It Combines Conservative Nationalism With Centrist Adaptability, Allowing It To Absorb Elements Of Neoliberalism, Populist Conservatism, And Regional Development Politics While Maintaining A Broad Anti-Left Consensus.
